rationale: Introduce one owned Pin<Box<_>> at the common nested preregistered await. The child future is then polled through a pointer rather than being stored inline in the parent future. This is the narrowest shared fixture boundary selected after the actual layout diagnostic and an independent static peer review.
limits: Box::pin first receives the constructed future and then moves it into a Box; a construction temporary can still occupy stack.
No claim is made that peak stack falls by the future's static size or that this alone fixes all 13 failures.

PanelFixture::completed subsequently awaits two completed_member futures while retaining original and completed member values. If another state variant determines its maximum layout, boxing only the first preregistered await may not reduce the outer future size at all.
This does not rewrite a recursive algorithm, change any production owner, or create another runtime/thread/task.
Only the original same future is awaited once. Its output tuple, locals, order, error propagation, cancellation and drop responsibility remain the same.
The integrated V2 metadata and original fixes must be verified together at one final source.
